Article Title: "Take that cross off your neck": Fans trash Sophie Cunningham over Sydney Sweeney comments as WNBA debate intensifies
Article Text:
Sophie Cunningham questions Sydney Sweeney’s controversial ad

Sophie Cunningham’s comments spark divided fan reactions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sophie Cunningham has weighed in on Sydney Sweeney ’s controversial sports betting ad, but the reaction online has become a story of its own. While the Indiana Fever guard questioned the campaign’s authenticity and raised concerns about its message, some fans rushed to defend Sweeney. Others turned the discussion into a debate about women in sports, beauty standards and why the ad drew so much attention.Cunningham shared her thoughts on Sweeney’s Novig campaign during the premiere of her revamped podcast, No Hesitation, which she co-hosts with Drew Hanlen. The ad features Sweeney appearing nude while trying different sports and repeating the phrase, “Just sports.”Cunningham questioned whether Sweeney genuinely follows sports betting and described the campaign as inauthentic. Still, she made it clear that her criticism of the ad did not mean she disliked the actress.“I have so many takes,” Cunningham said. “First of all, like, does she even gamble on sports? Like, it’s just so inauthentic. You know what I mean? Am I surprised of how she represented the brand? No. That’s what she’s made her whole career off — and, hey, don’t get me wrong. I like her. Everyone knows she is beautiful; she is hot. She clearly has my chest.”Cunningham also acknowledged Sweeney’s right to make her own choices, adding, “I really like her,” before explaining that the campaign was not to her taste.Hanlen suggested Sweeney was following a familiar marketing approach, pointing to her previous American Eagle campaign. Cunningham then questioned why women were particularly upset, given that the ad appeared to target men.“But why are girls mad?” Cunningham said. “That is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad? It is a gambling ad. Men, sports, pretty much naked women. Like, of course, that’s gonna draw attention. Again, do I agree with it? Morally, I think it’s kind of weird, but to each their own. Go do your thing, sis.”She later stressed that she did not believe the campaign was intended to undermine women in sports. Cunningham also praised athletes who challenge traditional beauty standards and encourage young girls to embrace their bodies.Cunningham’s take quickly became a talking point online, with fans split over whether Sweeney’s ad deserved criticism or was simply another marketing campaign.One commenter argued that the ad was simply doing what sports betting promotions are designed to do, writing, “It’s a sports betting ad look at it for what it is. No different that beer ads or hooters girls and chicken. Its has nothing to do with Women sports”Another added, "Sophie, please take that cross off your neck. I know exactly what you’re, nothing but a puppet for the elite. You stand for absolutely nothing and believe that God made you tall so you could play basketball. Full blown hypocrite."Another fan suggested jealousy was driving the backlash, claiming, “The ones that are mad are just jealous. That's all. It is just like all the women in the WNBA. It's pure jealousy. They don't know how to handle it and so they act like children”Others took a more provocative approach. One user wrote, “Threesome with Cunningham and Sweeney would be the ultimate dream,” while another commented, “Sidney is hotter than fish grease. She can’t help herself.”Some reactions focused on the campaign’s political and cultural implications. One commenter wrote, “Because she’s white. If she was black nobody would complain. Weird agenda type shit”Another fan suggested a joint campaign featuring both women, posting, “Now do an ad with Sophie AND Sydney in it together! The libal lefts heads will explode like in that movie Scanners 🤣🤣🤣🤣”Not every response focused on the controversy. One user questioned the promotion itself, writing, “Why is nobody talking about the $25 credit? It's sad. $200 in the average.”The comments show how Cunningham’s remarks have sparked a broader online argument about advertising, women in sports and public reactions to Sweeney’s campaign. While fans remain divided, the debate has pushed the Novig ad far beyond its original sports betting pitch.
Article Summary: Sophie cunningham questioned sydney sweeney’s controversial sports betting ad. The indiana fever guard questioned whether sweeney genuinely follows sports betting. Some fans rushed to defend sweeney, while others turned the discussion into a debate about women in sports and beauty standards.

Article Title: From Erling Haaland and Kai Rooney to Mikel Arteta’s son Gabriel, meet the football wonderkids following the footsteps of their famous parents
Article Text:
Erling Haaland with his family (via Gabrielle Haaland/Instagram)

From Kai Rooney to Phoenix Offiah, exploring how the next generation is making its mark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Becoming a professional footballer requires talent, dedication and years of hard work. But for some young players, football is already part of their family history. Several youngsters are now trying to follow in the footsteps of famous parents who made their mark in sport. Erling Haaland is one of the biggest examples after following his father Alf-Inge Haaland into professional football. The Premier League and its academies also feature several other youngsters with famous sporting or celebrity parents. From Kai Rooney to Gabriel Arteta, these rising talents are now looking to build careers of their own.One of the most recognisable names on the list is Kai Rooney, the eldest son of Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney and Coleen Rooney. The 16-year-old is following his father’s path at Manchester United and recently signed scholarship terms with the club.Kai has already featured for United’s Under-18 side. He scored two goals and provided an assist in seven appearances last season. The teenager has also revealed that he models his game on former Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli.Kai faces obvious comparisons with his father. His middle name is also Wayne, making the connection even stronger.Another youngster attracting attention is Kingston Haye, the 12-year-old son of former boxing world champion David Haye.Kingston is part of Arsenal’s academy after joining Hale End from Sutton last year.The youngster impressed scouts with his technical ability, vision and ball control. His father’s sporting background is not the only connection to athletics in the family. Kingston’s older brother Cassius, 18, has also competed on the junior tennis circuit in Spain.Former England striker Emile Heskey is also seeing his sons make progress in football. His sons Reigan and Jaden both came through the Manchester City academy.Jaden Heskey, 20, has spent time on loan at Sheffield Wednesday after impressing during an earlier spell. Reigan, 18, left Manchester City permanently this summer and joined German club Cologne.At Tottenham, Phoenix Offiah is another youngster carrying a famous sporting surname. The 16-year-old is the son of rugby league legend Martin Offiah.Phoenix has impressed in Tottenham’s academy and has been tipped for an England youth call-up. The 6ft 2in striker scored all four goals in a 4-1 win over Wolves last month and has also trained with Roberto De Zerbi’s first-team squad.Gabriel Arteta, son of Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, is another name to watch. Gabriel became a first-year scholar this summer and has already represented Arsenal Under-18s.Meanwhile, football is also part of the lives of Madonna’s adopted twin daughters Stella and Estere Ciccone. The 14-year-olds are enrolled in Tottenham Women’s youth ranks and have attended WSL matches with their mother.These youngsters have famous family names behind them, but their progress on the pitch will ultimately shape their own football careers!
Article Summary: From kai rooney to phoenix offiah, the next generation is making its mark in football. Erling haaland is one of the biggest examples after following his father into professional football. The premier league and its academies also feature several other youngsters with famous sporting or celebrity parents.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “My family kept me grounded when the whole world was screaming my name.” - How Ryan Coleman-Williams turned unconditional family backing into college football superstardom
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “My family kept me grounded when the whole world was screaming my name.” - How Ryan Coleman-Williams turned unconditional family backing into college football superstardom

How Ryan Coleman-Williams and Ryan Williams Sr. built their football connection

Why Ryan Williams reclassified from 2025 to 2024

What Ryan Williams did at Alabama at only 17

How Ryan Williams’ family stayed part of his rise

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ryan Coleman-Williams was already one of the biggest names in Alabama high school football when he made a decision that changed his path. The Saraland star left high school a year early, moved from the 2025 recruiting class to 2024 and joined Alabama at just 17. The move came with plenty of attention, but his family had been part of his football journey long before he reached Tuscaloosa. His father, Ryan Williams Sr., had played college football, while his mother, Tiffany Coleman, and his grandparents helped give him the support and structure he needed from a young age.Football was familiar territory in the Williams family. Ryan Williams Sr. played at Auburn after a standout high school career at B.C. Rain in Mobile. He later transferred to Copiah-Lincoln Community College and finished his college career at Louisiana Tech. His playing career gave him a clear understanding of the demands that came with trying to reach the next level.But Ryan Coleman-Williams’ development was not only about his father’s football background. ESPN reported that Williams lived with his paternal grandparents, Robert and Catherine Williams, while his father was away at college.His mother, Tiffany Coleman, also spoke about the role the family played in shaping his personality.“He’s an old soul,” Coleman told ESPN. “People are like, ‘He’s so mature to be 17.’ His grandparents had a lot to do with that. His maturity and foundation came from them.”That family support became especially important as Williams’ football career began moving faster than most teenagers could imagine.At Saraland High School, he became one of the most productive players in the state. Alabama’s official profile says he had 198 receptions for 3,486 yards and 49 receiving touchdowns during his high school career. He also rushed for 1,082 yards and 25 touchdowns.Williams originally belonged to the 2025 recruiting class. He had already committed to Alabama, but in 2023 he and his family decided that he would finish high school early and join the Crimson Tide sooner than planned.The decision was not made suddenly. ESPN reported that Williams told Saraland coach Jeff Kelly about the move in July 2023, although the decision was kept private while the team continued its season. Williams officially announced the reclassification in December.Kelly said the family handled the decision carefully because Williams did not want it to become a distraction for his teammates.“I think it speaks volumes about who he is,” Kelly told ESPN. “He didn’t want it to be out there because he didn’t want it to be a distraction for his teammates. We had a team that had a chance to win another state title. He and his family did a tremendous job keeping that decision private.”The timing also made sense from a football point of view. Williams had already achieved almost everything possible at the high school level. In 2023, he helped Saraland win another Class 6A state title and finished his high school career with huge numbers.The Alabama Sports Writers Association later named him Mr. Football for the second straight year, making him the first two-time winner of the award.Joining Alabama meant stepping into a completely different level of football. Williams was only 17 during his freshman season, while competing against players who were several years older.He showed that the age gap did not stop him.In September 2024, Williams caught a 75-yard touchdown pass from Jalen Milroe against Georgia in front of more than 100,000 fans at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Alabama won 41-34, and the play became one of the defining moments of Williams’ first college season.Alabama’s official records from that season show just how fast he adjusted. He finished his freshman campaign with 48 catches for 865 yards and eight touchdowns, according to the university’s later player profile. He also earned freshman All-America recognition.The early success was not completely unexpected. Before he even played a college game, Alabama had already listed Williams as a five-star recruit and one of the country’s top receiving prospects. The university said he was among the five-star players added to its 2024 recruiting class.The numbers tell only part of Williams’ story. His family had been around him throughout the long process that took him from Saraland to Alabama.That was clear when he officially signed with Alabama in February 2024. Local outlet Call News published a photograph of Williams with his father Ryan Sr., mother Tiffany Coleman, grandmother Catherine Williams and stepmother Cortney Williams at the signing ceremony.His grandmother has also spoken about how unusual his focus was even as a young child. She recalled that when Williams was in kindergarten, he was already eager to help teachers while other children were playing.That same focus later showed up on the football field.Williams did not have to wait until college to become a star. At Saraland, he won Alabama Mr. Football twice and became one of the most closely watched high school players in the state. His family then supported a difficult decision to leave school early and take on college football at an age when most players are still preparing for their final high school season.That is what makes Ryan Williams’ rise from Saraland to Alabama especially striking. His story is not only about spectacular catches or becoming a college football name at 17. It is also about a young player making an unusually early jump while having his parents, grandparents and family around him throughout the process.
Article Summary: Ryan coleman-williams was one of the biggest names in alabama high school football. The saraland star left high school a year early, moved from the 2025 recruiting class to 2024. His father, ryan williams sr. had played college football, while his mother, tiffany coleman, and his grandparents helped give him the support and structure he needed.

Article Title: Lauren Steadman: How Paralympic gold led to Celebrity MasterChef glory, career, net worth and personal life in focus
Article Text:
Lauren Steadman: How Paralympic gold led to Celebrity MasterChef glory, career, net worth and personal life in focus

How did Lauren Steadman win Celebrity MasterChef 2026 with Emily Campbell and Shakira Khan

What are Lauren Steadman’s Paralympic achievements and sports records

What is Lauren Steadman’s net worth, education and personal life

Lauren Steadman has added another major title to a career already filled with Paralympic medals. The British athlete won Celebrity MasterChef 2026 after beating Olympic weightlifter Emily Campbell and Love Island star Shakira Khan in the BBC One final. Steadman impressed judges Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli with a three-course menu, with her sticky toffee pudding playing an important part in the decision. The victory gives the 33-year-old another television success after Strictly Come Dancing and Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins. But away from TV, Steadman’s biggest achievements have come in swimming and paratriathlon.Steadman won the Celebrity MasterChef 2026 final on September 18 after the three finalists were asked to cook a three-course meal for Dent and Locatelli. The series started with 15 celebrities before the competition was reduced to the final three.Her menu began with pan-fried scallops in chilli butter, served with coconut and spinach lentil dahl puree and fresh apple batons. For the main course, she prepared beef Wellington with truffle mash, caramelised shallots, butternut squash puree, tenderstem broccoli and red wine jus.The dessert was a classic sticky toffee pudding with dates, caramel sauce and clotted cream ice cream.It proved to be a key moment in the final. Locatelli praised the pudding, while Dent also spoke highly of Steadman’s food.Steadman was visibly emotional after hearing the result. She said: “This is up there with a Paralympic gold medal. There haven’t been many moments when I have been left speechless but this is one of them.”The final followed several demanding challenges during the series. Steadman had already cooked for guests at Crufts and taken part in the Chef’s Table at The Ritz.Steadman’s final menu helped her secure the trophy, while also noting her earlier Paralympic success.Before becoming a television regular, Steadman built her name in elite sport. Born in Peterborough, she started swimming at a young age and represented Great Britain at the Beijing 2008 Paralympic Games when she was 15.She returned to the pool at London 2012. Her results did not bring a Paralympic medal, but the experience helped shape what came next.Steadman later moved into paratriathlon after her uncle, who is also a triathlete, encouraged her to try the sport. Her first British triathlon came in 2011, when she finished second.Her first Paralympic triathlon medal came at Rio 2016, where she won silver in the sport’s Paralympic debut. Five years later, she went one step further at Tokyo 2020, winning gold in the women’s PTS5 event.At Paris 2024, Steadman returned to the podium with bronze in the same classification. That gave her a full set of Paralympic triathlon medals: silver, gold and bronze.According to ParalympicsGB, Steadman is a three-time World Champion and has won eight European titles. She was also appointed MBE in the 2022 New Year Honours for services to triathlon.Steadman’s television career began long before Celebrity MasterChef. In 2018, she joined Strictly Come Dancing with professional dancer AJ Pritchard. She reached the semi-finals and became the first female contestant with a disability to take part in the BBC show.Her next major television challenge came with Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins. Steadman reached the final stage of the competition and was later crowned a joint winner of the series.She also appeared on Richard Osman’s House of Games before taking on Celebrity MasterChef in 2026.The television appearances have given audiences a different look at Steadman outside competition. Strictly tested her dancing, SAS put her through demanding physical and mental challenges, while MasterChef moved her into a completely different setting.Her professional work also includes motivational speaking and business activity. Steadman’s official website describes her work around mindset, performance and helping people deal with perceived barriers. She is also linked to Sizu, a motivational wellness clothing brand.According to LatestCelebArticles, Lauren Steadman’s net worth is estimated at between $1 million and $5 million. However, the website does not provide financial records or details showing how the figure was calculated, so the estimate cannot be independently confirmed. Her income is linked to her sporting career, television appearances, sponsorships and other professional work.The University of Portsmouth’s profile of the Paralympic champion confirms that, alongside her sporting and television career, she has also been involved in entrepreneurial work.Her income has come from several areas over the years, including elite sport, television work, sponsorships, speaking engagements and business projects. Her exact earnings from Celebrity MasterChef and her other television appearances have not been publicly disclosed.Steadman also has a strong academic background. She studied Psychology at the University of Portsmouth, graduating with a first-class degree in 2014. She later completed an MSc in Business and Management with distinction in 2017.The University of Portsmouth has highlighted both degrees in its profiles of Steadman. The university also notes her sporting achievements, including her Rio silver, Tokyo gold and Paris bronze.Away from sport and television, Steadman has generally kept her personal life private. She has spoken publicly about the role her family played in her early sporting journey, while her uncle was the person who encouraged her to try triathlon after her swimming career.Claims about her current relationship should be treated carefully because reliable public sources do not provide enough information to independently confirm the reported details about a boyfriend named Danny.Steadman has built a career across several very different fields. She went from a teenage Paralympic swimmer to a world-class paratriathlete, won gold at Tokyo 2020, returned for bronze in Paris, appeared on major British television shows and has now added the Celebrity MasterChef trophy to her record.
Article Summary: Lauren steadman won celebrity masterchef 2026 on september 18. She beat olympic weightlifter emily campbell and love island star shakira khan in the bbc one final. Steadman impressed judges grace dent and giorgio locatelli with a three-course menu, with her sticky toffee pudding playing an important part in the decision.

Why the Gisele Bundchen and Tom Brady story still matters for modern marriages

Long before "work-life balance" became a boardroom buzzword, one of football's greatest champions was learning that lesson at his own kitchen table. Back in 2020, Tom Brady opened up about a letter from his wife, Gisele Bundchen , that changed how he showed up at home. Their story still resonates today, offering a timeless reminder about partnership, fairness, and what it really takes to keep a marriage strong.Speaking with radio host Howard Stern, Brady recalled a moment from 2018 that forced him to rethink his priorities. Gisele had written him a letter laying out her frustration. She felt like the football season would end, and instead of turning his attention home, Brady would dive straight into business deals and offseason training.“She didn’t feel like I was doing my part for our family,” he said. “She felt like I would play football all season and she would take care of the house and all of a sudden when the season would end, I would be like, ‘Great, let me get into all my other business activities. Let me get into my football training.’ And she’s sitting there going, ‘Well, when are you going to do things for the house? When are you going to take the kids to school and do that?’”Brady didn't sugarcoat how that realization hit him. He admitted, "I had to, like, check myself." His wife had made her point clearly. She had goals of her own too, and she wasn't willing to put them on hold indefinitely while he chased his.That single letter pushed Brady to skip a few team activities so he could be more present at home, whether that meant school runs or simply being around for his kids. It's a small shift on paper, but for a professional athlete at the peak of his career, it spoke volumes.This isn't just a celebrity anecdote. Women still shoulder a disproportionate share of unpaid household work compared to men, according to research from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.That imbalance, valued in the trillions of dollars annually, shows up in ordinary homes just as much as in the households of millionaires.Melinda Gates faced a similar dynamic in her own marriage. When her daughter started kindergarten, Melinda wanted to wait a year because of a long commute. Bill insisted on enrolling her right away, then asked what would make it easier. Her answer was simple: he could drive.Brady's takeaway echoed that same lesson about partnership. He put it plainly: relationships only work when both people benefit, not just one. Years later, his words still hold up as a reminder that even the busiest, most successful people have to make room for the people they love.
Article Summary: Tom brady opened up about a letter from his wife, gisele bundchen, that changed how he showed up at home. Their story still resonates today, offering a timeless reminder about partnership, fairness, and what it really takes to keep a marriage strong.

Alonzo Menifield's thumb injury and the reaction inside the arena

Alonzo Menifield was supposed to be the next name on Iwo Baraniewski's knockout list. The 38-year-old had other plans on Saturday night at UFC 331, and a hand injury that made an entire arena groan did not change them.The light heavyweight bout opened the main card at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. Baraniewski, an undefeated Polish fighter with a habit of finishing early, had never needed the judges before. Menifield, a veteran with a dozen UFC wins, changed that and collected the win.Alonzo Menifield and Iwo Baraniewski met on Saturday, September 19, and the first round belonged to the Polish fighter. Baraniewski, riding a run of first-round knockouts, stunned Menifield more than once with his right hook and put the 38-year-old on the mat. Menifield gave up his back but survived, then found his footing in a late scramble, according to LowKick MMA's round-by-round account.Round two followed a similar script. Menifield started fast and landed heavy shots. Baraniewski kept walking forward anyway and found the cleaner combinations.Before round three, the doctor took a look at Menifield's hand. MMA Junkie described a deep cut, and the fight went on. The veteran opened the final round by stunning Baraniewski, but both men were tired by then.They spent long stretches in the clinch until the referee split them up. After the restart, Baraniewski pushed the pace and landed the harder strikes until the bell.The scorecards told a tight story. Two judges gave it 29-28 to Menifield, and one went 28-29 the other way. It was Baraniewski's first career loss and his first trip to a decision, which left the Polish fighter at 9-1.The full extent of the damage only came out after the decision was read. During the post-fight interview with Joe Rogan , Menifield held the thumb up to the camera. The Big Lead reported that a bone was sticking through, and MMA Junkie said the crowd let out a loud groan.The reports do not agree on when it happened. The Big Lead placed the injury in the first round, while MMA Junkie pointed to the doctor's check ahead of round three. LowKick MMA called it a broken thumb and said Menifield fought through it in the third.Fans did not need long to react. Barstool Sports posted, "Alonzo Menifield’s thumb is backwards and he’s still letting it fly" (@barstoolsports). Championship Rounds wrote, "ALONZO MENIFIELD'S THUMB HAS A BONE STICKING OUT" (@ChampRDS).The Big Lead reported that Menifield will not be back in action anytime soon, and none of the three reports give a recovery timeline. The 38-year-old is now 19-6-1 with 11 knockouts and has won two straight.
Article Summary: Alonzo menifield beats iwo baraniewski despite injury. The 38-year-old is now 19-6-1 with 11 knockouts and has won two straight. The full extent of the damage only came out after the decision was read.

Article Title: Japan opens Asian Games 2026 with a heartfelt celebration of culture and unity in Aichi-Nagoya
Article Text:
Nagoya wows the continent

Who will open India’s medal tally?

NAGOYA: Almost three hours before the start of the Asian Games opening ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, spectators had begun filling the expansive, multi-tiered stands. The 35,000-capacity venue was not full, but that did little to dampen the celebration that followed.The first glimpse was of a gigantic heart. But this was not merely about love. The heart-shaped stage, bathed in white, underlined the ceremony’s theme — Harmonic Hea-rtbeat. Like matcha, sake or sushi, themes and cultures can be an acquired taste. Whi-le some found the nearly two-hour spectacle underwhelming, from a Japanese perspective it was a celebration steeped in tradition, culture, diversity and technology.The evening began with a pre-ceremony performance by the Shigo Bonote Preservation Society and the hugely popular INI boy band. The ceremony itself opened with dancers in heart-shaped attire and a performance by celebrated Japanese violinist Taro Hakase. With Japanese royalty led by emperor Naruhito and empress Masako, International Olympic Committee president Kirsty Coventry and Olympic Council of Asia president Sheikh Joaan Hamad Al Thani among the dignitaries in attendance, the Japanese national flag was raised by members of the Japan Self-Defence Forces.Volunteers carrying heart-shaped placards bearing the names of participating countries then led the athletes and officials into the stadium. The Indians, looking dapper in deep blue, received a warm welcome, though the loudest cheers in the stadium were reserved for the hosts.The centrepiece of the night was a replica of Nagoya Castle, placed at the heart of the stage and illuminated in a kaleidoscope of colours.The heart-shaped cauldron was lit by five-time Asian Games champion and hammer throw legend Shigenobu Murofushi and his son Koji, the 2004 Olympic hammer throw champion.Sheikh Joaan in his speech said, “Tonight, the eyes of Asia and much of the world turn to Japan. What we will see over the next few days will inspire us. It will move us. And it will remind us of what we are capable of when we come together for Asia.”With One Asia, One Heart at the centre of the ceremony, the troubles of the past few days, which had put Nagoya’s ability to host the Games under scrutiny, seemed to fade into the background, at least for the night.The ceremony ended with fireworks lighting up the night sky, offering a fitting hope that the Games, too, will shine as brightly.India, who returned from the 2022 Hangzhou Games with a record 107 medals, will begin their quest to better that haul on Sunday, with three disciplines offering early opportunities to get on the board.All eyes will be on the Aichi Prefectural Shooting Ra-nge, with India expected to be in the thick of action, fighting for a podium finish. Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod will comp-ete in the women’s 10m air rif-le, with medals at stake in bo-th the team and individual ev-ents. In women’s cricket, defe-nding champions India face Bangladesh in the semifinal. A win will assure India of a m-edal. There could also be an interesting twist to India’s medal-opening narrative. In teqball, two bronze medals are up for grabs, while Suraj Singh will compete in the men’s changquan event, a medal event on the day, in wushu.
Article Summary: Nagoya wows the continent with two-hour spectacle. From a japanese perspective it was a celebration steeped in tradition, culture, diversity and technology. India, who returned from the 2022 hangzhou games with a record 107 medals, will begin their quest to better that haul on sunday.

Article Title: "She’s trying to be the general manager of the team": How Bill Belichick finally addressed Jordon Hudson’s UNC role and called one major assumption “so ridiculous”
Article Text:
Bill Belichick breaks his silence on Jordon Hudson’s UNC role (Getty Images)

What did Bill Belichick say about Jordon Hudson’s role at UNC?

Does Jordon Hudson have an official role with UNC football?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bill Belichick has finally offered a fuller explanation of Jordon Hudson’s role around his move to North Carolina, pushing back on the idea that she had influence over the Tar Heels’ football operation. In an interview with The Wall Street Journal, Belichick said Hudson helped coordinate parts of his schedule outside the university but had no official role with UNC football. He also took direct aim at a narrative that portrayed her as trying to control the program, calling that suggestion “so ridiculous.” The comments give Belichick’s clearest account yet of how a personal scheduling request became a much bigger story.Bill Belichick said the confusion began when he joined North Carolina and was still juggling several commitments away from coaching. At the time, he was working on television projects, a radio show and a book while taking charge of the Tar Heels.That workload led him to ask UNC staff to send requests related to his personal appearances to Hudson so she could help coordinate them separately from his university responsibilities.“When I took the job here, it was December, and at that time I was doing five TV shows, the radio show, I had a book coming out. I had a lot of other things going on when I took the job,” Belichick said.He said that request was later presented in a very different light.“So, I sent an email when I got here and I said, 'Can you please forward any requests to Jordon about my personal appearances so that I can work and coordinate them outside the university?' Didn't have anything to do with the university. Well, that was leaked and released as 'Jordon's involved in every single thing that I do and she's copied on every email.' That's just a flat-out lie.”Belichick was even more blunt when discussing the suggestion that Hudson wanted power within the football program.“The way the story was picked up was a long way from that. Like, 'She's trying to be the general manager of the team,' and it's so ridiculous.”According to Belichick, she does not. He made a distinction between helping with parts of his life away from North Carolina football and having a role inside the program.“There are some things that she helps me schedule or look at,” he said. “It's not North Carolina stuff.”That clarification matters because Hudson’s presence around Belichick had previously generated questions about how much access or influence she had around the Tar Heels. Belichick had also publicly said in 2025 that Hudson had no role with the UNC football program.Hudson has remained largely out of the public discussion surrounding UNC this season. The Tar Heels opened the 2026 campaign 2-0 under Belichick before their ACC matchup with Clemson, keeping the focus increasingly on football rather than the off-field questions that followed the coach during his first season.For Belichick, though, the issue was worth addressing again because he believes a simple request tied to his personal schedule was turned into something much larger. His latest comments draw a clear boundary: Hudson may assist him with personal matters, but he says that should not be confused with running, influencing or managing UNC football.
Article Summary: Bill belichick breaks his silence on jordon hudson’s unc role. Belichick said the confusion began when he joined north carolina and was still juggling several commitments away from coaching. At the time, he was working on television projects, a radio show and a book while taking charge of the tar heels.

Article Title: “This was suppose to be the future Jon Jones?” Fans let out their true feelings about Sean Sharaf's stunning win at UFC 331
Article Text:
Sean Sharaf scores stunning KO over Gable Steveson. Image via: Cooper Neill/Zuffa LLC

Sean Sharaf defeats Gable Steveson at UFC 331 in just 12 seconds

Sean Sharaf quotes Nate Diaz following his victory

UFC fans react to Sean Sharaf's win as Jon Jones looks speechless

Sean Sharaf needed just 12 seconds to flip UFC 331 on its head. One left hook from the former Marine dropped Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson at Crypto.com Arena, and the referee stopped the fight before the crowd had time to settle.Nobody expected this script. Steveson arrived as a heavy favorite with an unbeaten record, wrestling prowess, and Jon Jones in his corner. Sharaf had other plans, and the fallout hit social media within minutes. Fans were loud, blunt, and often very funny.Sean Sharaf beat Gable Steveson by first-round knockout on Saturday night in Los Angeles, and the whole thing took 12 seconds. The heavyweight bout sat on the UFC 331 main card, and few people saw a finish that quick coming.It came down to one exchange. Sharaf pushed forward from the opening bell and forced Steveson to give ground. Steveson dodged a right hand, but the miss left him open. Sharaf answered with a left hook that landed flush at the 10-second mark and dropped him. A few ground shots followed, and the referee stopped it at 12 seconds.Steveson entered as a -2400 favorite, backed by his Olympic gold medal in wrestling and a 4-0 record.Sharaf, a former United States Marine, was a +1500 underdog. He is now 5-2-0. Steveson drops to 4-1-0, and this is his first loss as an MMA fighter.Sharaf brought up Steveson's past at the pre-fight press conference, and the two went back and forth. The crowd booed Steveson loudly that day, which made it clear who fans were backing. He had Jones and coach Greg Jackson in his corner, yet neither could change what happened. Steveson did get up and talk with his corner and the officials who checked on him. He left the octagon before Bruce Buffer could read the official result."The Smoke" broke down in tears inside the octagon once the result sank in. Then the mood flipped. During his octagon interview with Joe Rogan , Sharaf opened by borrowing Nate Diaz's famous line about not being surprised, expletive and all. Diaz first used it after handing Conor McGregor his first UFC defeat. The Crypto.com Arena crowd went wild.Sharaf then turned to the people who doubted him. "I believed in myself when nobody believed in me," he said. He also thanked the fans for their support and energy, and said he had worked hard and prayed hard for this night.The win also put his name in the record books. His 12-second finish is the third-quickest knockout in the heavyweight division. Between that result and the Diaz moment, Sharaf has gained plenty of new eyes. If the wins keep coming, his dream of ruling the division someday looks a little closer.Jon Jones spent the night in Steveson's corner, and the cameras found him right after the finish. He looked stunned, then worried, as chaos filled the arena around him. Jones is both a friend and a coach to Steveson, and the two had predicted a heavyweight title fight for the Olympic gold medalist in the near future. This loss may have put that plan on hold, at least for now.Fans noticed the look on Jones's face too, and many did not hold back.Rob Kuhn (@RobKuhn_) posted: "this was suppose to be the future jon Jones?"World in Motion (@WorldInMotionHQ) went after the build-up: "Rogan spent weeks warning heavyweights about Steveson and it took Sharaf 12 seconds to make that warning look like a bad take"Ava Brown (@AvaBrownddbz) wrote: "Sharaf ending Stevenson's Olympic-to-cage hype in 12 seconds is the fastest anyone's changed my mind on a 'future champ' tag this year"Mr. Antiquated (@MrAntiquated) added: "Credit to anyone getting in the cage but I thought everyone said Gable was going to be some unstoppable force."LuckyRebel (@RBLOfficial_) kept it short: "I’ve had sips of water that lasted longer."Fans’ roasts were stronger as Steveson was the favorite to win for many.

The fallout hit social media within minutes, and fans were loud, blunt and often very funny. Rogan spent weeks warning heavyweights about steveson and it took sharaf 12 seconds to make that warning look like a bad take.

India opened their shooting campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with a silver medal in the women's 10m air rifle team event on Sunday, with Elavenil Valarivan , Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod combining for a second-place finish.The Indian trio accumulated 1898.0 points to take silver, finishing behind China, who claimed the gold with a world-record score of 1904.2 points. Hosts Japan secured the bronze after scoring 1897.1.The result marked India's first confirmed medal of the 20th Asian Games at Aichi-Nagoya. MMA fighter Suchika Tariyal had earlier become the first Indian athlete to assure a medal after progressing to the semifinals of the women's Traditional MMA 60kg competition, where both losing semifinalists receive bronze.Sonam emerged as India's highest scorer in the team event, registering 634.1 points. Elavenil contributed 633.5, while Vidarsa finished with 630.4 as the Indian team crossed the 1898-point mark.There was further reason for India to celebrate as Elavenil and Sonam also secured places in the individual final. Their scores were enough to put both shooters among the eight finalists for the individual 10m air rifle competition.The two Indians will now have another opportunity to add to the country's medal tally when they compete in the eight-woman individual final later on Sunday. Having already stood on the podium in the team event, Elavenil and Sonam will be aiming for another strong showing in the individual competition.The silver also gives India's shooting contingent an encouraging beginning at the Games, particularly after the country's shooters enjoyed a highly successful campaign at the Hangzhou Asian Games.India's shooting team returned from Hangzhou with a record haul of 22 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and six bronze. The Aichi-Nagoya campaign has now begun with another silver, with the Indian shooters set for more medal opportunities in the days ahead.

Sri Lanka Women stormed into the gold-medal match of the Asian Games 2026 women’s cricket tournament after captain Chamari Athapaththu produced a match-winning knock to guide her side to an eight-wicket victory over Pakistan in the first semi-final on Sunday.Chasing 178 at Korogi Sports Park, Sri Lanka reached 178/2 in 17.5 overs, sealing the win with 13 balls to spare. The victory guarantees Sri Lanka at least a silver medal, while Pakistan will compete in the bronze-medal match.After a delayed start, Pakistan recovered from an early setback through a strong partnership between Ayesha Zafar and Shawaal Zulfiqar. The pair added 115 runs to put Pakistan in a strong position before the team finished its 20 overs at 177/4.Sri Lanka’s chase was anchored by Athapaththu, who struck an unbeaten 83 off 50 balls. Her innings featured seven boundaries and six sixes as she took control of the contest after settling in. Imesha Dulani added 26 off 21 balls, helping Sri Lanka maintain momentum, while the captain continued to attack the Pakistan bowlers and guide her team towards the target.Pakistan struggled to contain Sri Lanka, with their bowling and fielding unable to halt the scoring. Sri Lanka eventually completed the chase in 17.5 overs, losing just two wickets.The win sends Sri Lanka into the gold-medal match, where they will face the winner of the second semi-final between India and Bangladesh. Pakistan, meanwhile, will take on the losing side in the bronze-medal playoff.
